result_text:
Suppliers now carry payment terms in days. A supplier registered without terms gets 30, and the terms are shown in the all-suppliers, by-country, by-minimum-rating and single-lookup results. The full offline test suite passes, including a new test for the 45-to-14-day example.

What changed:

- **`schema.sql`**: `supplier` gets `payment_terms_days INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30`, with a check that it is not negative.
- **`model/Supplier.java`**: new `paymentTermsDays` component. The existing 5-argument constructor defaults it to 30, so the 78 existing call sites compile unchanged.
- **`DataStore.java`**: `createSupplier` and `updateSupplier` write the terms. The three listings and `findSupplierById` read them. I also added them to the queries that embed a supplier (purchase suggestions, purchased quantity per supplier, supplier performance, spending per supplier, category suppliers). Without that, those results would have silently reported 30 days.
- **`SupplierTest.java`**: two new tests, one for the renegotiation example across all listings and the lookup, one for the 30-day default.

I did not change `DemoScenario`'s Nordic update. Its `run` method is already at the JVM 64 KB limit, and the extra argument broke compilation. Nordic never has terms set in the demo, so the default gives the same result.

Nothing is committed.
